transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I guess what really made me come in is the eating thing. Like, once I start, it feels like I hit some kind of switch and I just keep going, even while part of me is thinking, Dennis, just stop already.

It’s weird because I’ll be aware of it happening, but it’s like that doesn’t actually make me stop. I don’t know, it sounds kind of stupid saying it out loud. I mean, I’m in college classes right now—well, sort of, I’m not working or anything—and I can usually control myself with other stuff, but with this it just feels like I can’t get the brakes to work.
How often do these episodes happen? Like, do they happen at least once a week, and have they been going on for a few months or more?

Yeah, I think it’s most weeks. Like, since pretty early in the semester, it’ll usually happen one night, and then sometimes two if I’ve got deadlines or if there’s just a bunch of food around the apartment.

I guess it’s been pretty steady for… three or four months now? It kind of all blends with school stuff, but yeah, more than just a random couple times.
After these eating episodes, do you ever try to compensate for what you've eaten—like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or exercising a lot more than usual?

Um… I don’t know. Not really sure what counts as “compensate,” I guess. Like, I’ll feel awful and think I should do something, but then I usually just end up sitting there feeling gross or distracting myself.

I mean, sometimes I tell myself I’ll be better the next day, but that’s more like… I don’t know, making a plan in my head, not really doing some whole thing. Sorry, I’m kind of going in circles.
During these episodes, do you feel like you're not in control of your eating, like you can't stop once you start?

Yeah, that’s pretty much exactly it. Like once I start eating in that way, it feels like some switch flips and I just keep going, even if I’m literally thinking, “Dennis, stop, you don’t even want more.”  

It’s not like… I don’t know, deciding to have seconds at dinner or whatever. It’s more like I’m watching myself keep doing it and the “stop” thought is there, but it doesn’t actually do anything.
Do these eating episodes cause you a lot of distress, or do they interfere with your schoolwork, social life, or other parts of your day-to-day life?

Yeah, it bothers me a lot, honestly. Like, I’m not failing out or anything — I still go to class, and I still show up for robotics stuff. Actually robotics is kind of the one thing where I can pretend I’m normal because everyone’s just arguing about parts or code or whatever.

But the next morning after it happens, I’ll feel really sluggish and distracted, like I’m sitting in lecture but half my brain is still back in the kitchen thinking about it. And I waste time worrying if my roommates noticed food missing or heard me or are judging me. So it hasn’t totally derailed my life, but it’s definitely in my head more than I want it to be.
During these episodes, do you find yourself eating much more rapidly than normal?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t really notice it while it’s happening, but afterward it’s like, wait, how is all of that already gone?

A lot of times I’m standing at my desk, kind of half between homework and pulling up a game or something, and I’m just eating really fast, not even tasting it much. Like I’ll look down and it’s only been a few minutes, and the food is just… gone.
During these eating episodes, do you find yourself eating until you feel uncomfortably full?

Yeah, that happens. I usually don’t stop when I’m just full — it’s more like I stop when my stomach feels really tight and heavy, and then I’m sitting there like, why did I do that?

Sometimes I’ll be at my desk and I’m so uncomfortable sitting upright that I just want to go lie down for a while. Which is annoying because my desk chair already sucks, like the robotics lab chairs are somehow even worse, but… yeah, it’s not just the chair. It’s that I ate past the point where it felt okay.
Do you find yourself eating large amounts of food during these episodes even when you’re not actually hungry?

Yeah… not always because I’m hungry. Sometimes it’s more like the food is just there, or I’m kind of wiped out after a project deadline and I start eating and don’t really stop.

Like if there’s leftover pizza in the apartment, I can end up taking a whole small pizza back to my room, and then somehow chips and cereal too. Which is stupid because my roommates would just have, like, a normal amount for dinner and move on. And I’m sitting there with all these wrappers or bowls around me thinking, I wasn’t even that hungry when I started.
Do these eating episodes usually happen when you're feeling stressed, upset, or dealing with something negative, or do they happen more randomly?

I’m not totally sure. I mean, sometimes it probably is after I’m stressed, like if school stuff is piling up, but I don’t know if that’s the reason or if I’m just noticing it after.

Other times it feels kind of random, like I’m just in my room and food is there and then it turns into… that. It’s hard to separate it, honestly. Like college is kind of always stressful in the background, so I don’t know what counts.
Do you usually eat alone during these episodes because you're embarrassed about how much you're eating?

Yeah… I think so. Like, if my roommates are in the kitchen, I’ll eat a pretty normal amount, or at least try to make it look normal. Then later I’ll kind of grab more stuff and take it back to my room.

It’s not like I announce it or anything. I just don’t want them standing there watching me take, like, way more than everyone else. Which is dumb because they probably aren’t paying that much attention, but I feel like they are. So I’ll wait until no one’s around or I’ll just keep extra food in my room and eat it there.
Do you feel a lot of distress or concern about your body shape or weight, especially in relation to these eating episodes?

I don’t know… I mean, I’m not thrilled about it, obviously. But I don’t know if it’s like specifically my body shape or weight, if that makes sense.

Sometimes after it happens I’ll feel gross and kind of avoid thinking about it, but then I get distracted by classes or whatever. Like I’ll tell myself I should go to the gym, and then I remember the campus gym is always packed at weird times, especially with all the people who seem like they basically live there, and then I just don’t go.

So… yeah, I guess I’m concerned some, but I’m not sure how much of it is about my body versus just feeling bad that I did it.
During these eating episodes, do you feel like you're not in control of your eating — like you can't stop once you start?

Yeah. That’s kind of the main thing, honestly. Like once I start eating that way, it feels like I hit some switch or something, and then I just keep going even though part of me is like, Dennis, just stop already.

And it’s weird because before that I can be like, okay, I’ll just have a little bit, or I’ll just finish this one thing. But then it turns into more, and then I’m not really making normal decisions anymore. I mean, I am, but I’m also not. It’s like I’m watching myself keep doing it.
